public_rationale: He presents the figure as his own estimate ('I see around $22 billion'). The post gives no period, no definition of compute spend, and no method. The evidence search found no public source that measures global AI compute spending outside OpenAI and Anthropic. It also found that hyperscalers do not break out AI revenue by customer. Analyst estimates of the two labs' share differ widely, for example about 3% to 13% for AWS, according to search summaries. Testing the number would mean choosing a period and basis, such as one quarter or an annualized run rate, and the claim does not supply either. That choice could decide the result. Without a stated scope or a matching measure, the claim cannot be scored as supported or contradicted.
limitations: The packet contains no independent estimate of global AI compute spending outside OpenAI and Anthropic, on any basis.
The past analysis he refers to is not reproduced in the post, so the basis of his figure is unknown.
A later disclosure of customer-level AI cloud revenue could allow a rough check, but only if the period and basis he meant were known.
